sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 37.1 grams of fat. The bright spot is 5.8 grams of polyunsaturated fat, which helps balance the fat profile. The pressure point is 12.6 grams of saturated fat. For meats, fat quality matters because the protein can be good, but the fat decides how clean the tradeoff feels.

sections.title: Carbs
sections.narration: Carbs are basically out of the picture here. There are no defensible carb submacros to score, so this section does not really help or hurt bacon in the way it would for grains, fruits, or tubers.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 13.7 grams of protein. Essential amino acids land at 9 out of 9, so the protein has a real repair and maintenance role. Non-essential amino acids are also strong at 10 out of 11, while collagen is only 0.4 grams. For meats, protein quality is the main reason this entry stays interesting.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin B12 is the clear vitamin mark at 21% daily value, supporting nerves and blood cells. Vitamin D is only 1% daily value, and the rest of the vitamin panel is thin, so bacon is not carrying the broad micronutrient workload you might want from a meat.

closing.summary: So Bacon has real protein quality, useful vitamin B12, and a strong flavour role. But saturated fat, low vitamin D, low iron, heavy sodium, processing, and portions that are easy to overdo pull it down hard. It is best as a small flavour tool or occasional comfort-food add-on, not as a core everyday protein.
